quizName: DMV Practice Test #8 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean when riding in a group?

options.text: Speed up.
Danger ahead.
Stop.
Merge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: When a lead rider extends their left arm straight down with their palm facing back, group riders should stop. This is an important hand signal for group riding.

questions.question: What is true about motorcycle windshields?

options.text: They protect your eyes as well as a face shield.
They protect your eyes as well as goggles.
They will not protect your eyes from the wind.
They protect against items thrown from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They will not protect your eyes from the wind.
questions.explanation: A windshield is not a good substitute for a face shield or goggles. Most windshields do not protect your eyes from wind.

questions.question: Where should you find information specific to your motorcycle?

options.text: The owner's manual.
A general motorcycle book.
Someone who owns a different motorcycle model.
A television show about motorcycle riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: The owner's manual.
questions.explanation: Read your motorcycle's owner's manual before your first ride. This is especially important if you are riding a borrowed motorcycle. It gives you information about your specific motorcycle.

questions.question: How much following distance should you normally keep?

options.text: One second.
Two seconds.
Three seconds.
Four seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds.
questions.explanation: In normal conditions, keep at least two seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance when conditions are poor.

questions.question: What should your lane position help you do?

options.text: Show other drivers what you plan to do.
Stop other drivers from passing you.
Travel as fast as possible.
Stay in other drivers' blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Show other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: A good lane position protects your lane and shows other drivers what you intend to do next.

questions.question: When riding downhill or shifting to first gear, what may you need to do?

options.text: Slow down with your brakes before shifting to a lower gear.
Speed up before shifting to a lower gear.
Swerve to the left.
Tap your brakes to warn drivers behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down with your brakes before shifting to a lower gear.
questions.explanation: Slow to a safe speed with your brakes before shifting to a lower gear. Downshifting while going too fast can cause the motorcycle to jerk and the rear wheel to skid.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT protective clothing?

options.text: A leather jacket
Full-fingered gloves
Long denim pants
Athletic shoes

questions.correctAnswerText: Athletic shoes
questions.explanation: Leather jackets, long denim pants, and full-fingered gloves provide protection in a fall. Wear lace-up boots, high-top boots, or sturdy shoes with ankle support instead of athletic shoes.

questions.question: Your motorcycle weaves while riding over rain grooves or bridge gratings. What should you do?

options.text: Stay relaxed, keep your speed steady, and ride straight across.
Hold the grips tight and speed up to get past the hazard.
Zigzag across the surface.
Ride on the shoulder instead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay relaxed, keep your speed steady, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Weaving over rain grooves or bridge gratings is usually not dangerous. Relax and ride straight across at a steady speed. Zigzagging to correct the weaving is more dangerous than riding straight.

questions.question: What does a linked braking system do?

options.text: Connects the front and rear brakes so both brakes work when either is used.
Connects the front brake to the gear shifter.
Connects the rear brake to a foot control.
Connects the rear brake to a handlebar switch.

questions.correctAnswerText: Connects the front and rear brakes so both brakes work when either is used.
questions.explanation: A linked braking system connects the front and rear brakes. When you use either brake lever, both brakes get pressure applied. Check your owner's manual for details about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: Why is a cushion of space around your motorcycle helpful?

options.text: To give you time to react to hazards.
To hide you from other drivers.
To prevent you from avoiding hazards.
To let you read road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: To give you time to react to hazards.
questions.explanation: Space around your motorcycle gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake. You need this space to maneuver safely.

questions.question: Which should you NOT do to improve your safety when riding at night?

options.text: Increase your speed.
Reduce your speed.
Use your high beam headlight when possible.
Increase your following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your speed.
questions.explanation: To ride safely at night, reduce your speed, use your high beam headlight when no other vehicles are near, and increase your following distance. Watch vehicles ahead of you. Their headlights light up the road, and their taillights bounce if they hit bumps.

questions.question: The rear brake control is usually located:

options.text: On the right handlebar.
On the left handlebar.
Near the left foot.
Near the right foot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the right foot.
questions.explanation: The rear brake on a motorcycle is operated with your right foot.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding and you must stop, the best action is to:

options.text: Relax your grip on the handlebars.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Use both brakes and stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, grip the handlebars firmly, ease off the throttle, and keep the motorcycle straight. If you must brake, slowly apply the brake on the tire that is not flat. As you slow down, move to the side of the road, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: More than half of all crashes:

options.text: Involve riders with less than six months of experience on their motorcycle.
Are caused by faulty ignition systems.
Occur because passengers distract the rider.
Happen at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Involve riders with less than six months of experience on their motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Be extra careful when riding a motorcycle new to you. Most motorcycle crashes involve riders with less than six months of experience on that bike.

questions.question: A thorough check of your motorcycle:

options.text: Is useless unless a mechanic does it.
Should not be done before a ride.
Should be done only after a ride.
Can help you find mechanical problems or equipment failures.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can help you find mechanical problems or equipment failures.
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle thoroughly before every ride. This helps you find mechanical problems or equipment failures that could be dangerous.

questions.question: As a motorcycle operator, you can help others see you by:

options.text: Riding with your headlight off.
Wearing bright clothing.
Following other vehicles closely.
Not using turn signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wearing bright clothing.
questions.explanation: To be seen more easily, wear bright clothing, keep your headlight on at all times, and use your turn signals.

questions.question: When choosing footwear, you should select:

options.text: Shoes with long heels.
Shoes with long laces you cannot tuck in.
Shoes that cover your ankles.
Shoes made from flimsy materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shoes that cover your ankles.
questions.explanation: Wear boots or shoes that are high and sturdy enough to cover and support your ankles. Heels should be short so they do not catch on surfaces. Laces should be tucked in so they cannot catch on the motorcycle's moving parts.

questions.question: Riding alongside a car:

options.text: Is encouraged.
Can place you in a blind spot.
Is not a problem unless the road is wet.
Can make driving easier for the other driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can place you in a blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding directly next to another vehicle is dangerous because the driver may not see you. The vehicle also blocks your escape route.

questions.question: Increase your following distance:

options.text: If the road is slippery.
If there are only a few vehicles on the road.
If the sun is shining.
If drivers are following the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: If the road is slippery.
questions.explanation: You need more space if your motorcycle will take longer to stop. Increase your following distance if the pavement is slippery, if you cannot see through the vehicle ahead, or if traffic is heavy.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should travel:

options.text: More slowly than you would during the day under similar conditions.
At the same speed as you would during the day under similar conditions.
Faster than you would during the day under similar conditions.
On the road shoulder so other vehicles can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: More slowly than you would during the day under similar conditions.
questions.explanation: At night, travel slower than you would during the day under the same weather and traffic conditions. It is harder to see hazards in the dark, so slowing down helps you avoid dangers.

questions.question: What color are warning signs?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road hazards.

questions.question: What should you do when a driver is merging onto the highway from an entrance ramp?

options.text: Stay in your lane.
Merge into the next lane, if possible.
Not worry about it, since they are the ones trying to merge.
Ride on the far left shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge into the next lane, if possible.
questions.explanation: Give merging drivers space to enter safely. Move to another lane if you can. The merging driver may not see your motorcycle.

questions.question: What should you do to be more visible at an intersection?

options.text: Try to make eye contact with other drivers.
Ride with your headlight on.
Reduce your space cushion.
Ride in a weaving pattern.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride with your headlight on.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on at intersections. Position yourself where other drivers can see you. Never assume another driver sees you, even if you make eye contact.

questions.question: Where should you ride in your lane when you are about to pass another vehicle?

options.text: Ride in the right portion of the lane.
Ride in the left portion of the lane.
Get as close as possible to the vehicle in front of you.
Not signal your intentions, as that may distract the driver you are passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the left portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when passing. Signal before you pass. Check for traffic and pass only when it is safe. Signal again before returning to your original lane.

questions.question: Which is NOT a good reason to use your horn?

options.text: A driver in the lane next to you is too close to the vehicle ahead of them.
A parked car has a person in the driver's seat.
You want people to look at your motorcycle.
You are passing someone who is in the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: You want people to look at your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to alert pedestrians, cyclists, and drivers of your presence. Do not use it just to get attention. Sound your horn before passing vehicles or pedestrians that may move into your path.

questions.question: Do you need hearing protection when riding?

options.text: Not needed if you wear a helmet.
Needed in addition to a helmet.
Only needed on windy days.
Not needed if you are carrying a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Needed in addition to a helmet.
questions.explanation: Engine and wind noise can damage your hearing, even with a helmet. Hearing protection helps prevent this damage while still letting you hear important sounds like horns and sirens.

questions.question: How should a group of riders maintain closeness while staying safe?

options.text: In pairs.
In a staggered formation.
In a single-file line.
In a passing formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a staggered formation.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation keeps riders close while maintaining safe spacing. Use single-file when riding in curves, turning, or entering/leaving a highway. Never ride side-by-side.

questions.question: How do you control the accelerator on a motorcycle?

options.text: With the right hand
With the left hand
With the right foot
With the left foot

questions.correctAnswerText: With the right hand
questions.explanation: The accelerator is on the right handgrip. You control it with your right hand.

questions.question: Should you use your headlight during the day?

options.text: Not ride with your headlight on.
Ride with your headlight on, but only if it is cloudy.
Always ride with your headlight on.
Use your headlight if you think it helps.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always ride with your headlight on.
questions.explanation: Always use your headlight, even during the day. This makes you twice as likely to be seen by other drivers.

questions.question: Which provides the best eye protection?

options.text: Sunglasses
Windshield
Goggles
Face shield

questions.correctAnswerText: Face shield
questions.explanation: A plastic face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not adequate protection.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves when riding in a group?

options.text: In the front of the group.
Just behind the leader.
Close to the back of the group.
At the tail end of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This way, they won't fall behind the group. More experienced riders behind them can also watch out for them.

questions.question: When a driver makes eye contact with you, what does it mean?

options.text: Means that they see you.
Will never happen.
Does not mean that they will properly yield to you.
Guarantees that they will properly yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not mean that they will properly yield to you.
questions.explanation: Do not assume a driver will yield just because they look at you. Drivers often look directly at motorcyclists but fail to notice them.

questions.question: Which of the following will NOT help lower your chance of a crash?

options.text: Be visible.
Communicate your intentions.
Be prepared to react to hazards.
Hope another driver sees you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hope another driver sees you.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, you must be visible to other drivers and make your intentions clear through proper signaling and positioning. Maintain safe space around your motorcycle and watch for hazards ahead. Do not rely on hoping drivers will see you.

questions.question: Which sign is rectangular in shape?

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white backgrounds and black lettering. These signs show traffic rules you must follow.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up and lean the motorcycle.
Speed up and keep the motorcycle upright.
Slow down and lean the motorcycle.
Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as possible.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop quickly?

options.text: Use the front brake only.
Use the front brake first.
Throttle down and use the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.question: What is found in the center portion of a traffic lane?

options.text: Debris and oil drippings from cars often collect.
Motorcycle riders should always travel for safety.
Most accidents happen.
Drivers are least likely to see a motorcyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Debris and oil drippings from cars often collect.
questions.explanation: The center of a lane has debris and oil from cars. Hazards like utility hole covers are also found there.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks can affect a rider's ability to ride?

options.text: One
Three to four
Six
More than eight

questions.correctAnswerText: One
questions.explanation: Even one alcoholic drink can affect your riding ability. Riding under the influence of alcohol is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: When should you use both brakes?

options.text: Use only one brake if it is a non-emergency situation.
Only use both brakes if you are riding on wet pavement.
Use both brakes regardless of the circumstances.
Use only the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes regardless of the circumstances.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: How should you park a motorcycle next to a curb?

options.text: Parked at a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
Parked at a 45-degree angle with the front tire touching the curb.
Parked like a car, with the front and rear wheels the same distance from the curb.
Parked at the left edge of the parking space so approaching drivers can more easily see the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parked at a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
questions.explanation: Park your motorcycle at a 90-degree angle to the curb with your rear wheel touching it.

questions.question: Why are signals important on a motorcycle?

options.text: They don't matter much since motorcycles are small.
They warn other drivers about what you plan to do.
Use them only when other vehicles are nearby.
They are harder to use than on a car.

questions.correctAnswerText: They warn other drivers about what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Motorcyclists are at high risk. Always use turn signals when changing lanes or turning. Use them even if you think no one is nearby.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid danger, you should:

options.text: Do one action, then the other.
Do both actions at the same time.
Always brake first, then swerve.
Try to use only the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: Do braking and swerving separately. Brake then swerve, or swerve then brake. Never do both at the same time.

questions.question: What happens if your motorcycle's chain or belt breaks?

options.text: The rear wheel suddenly gets more power.
The rear wheel suddenly loses power.
The front wheel suddenly loses power.
The front wheel suddenly gets more power.

questions.correctAnswerText: The rear wheel suddenly loses power.
questions.explanation: If the chain or belt fails, power to the rear wheel stops immediately.

questions.question: You will ______ hear a tire going flat.

options.text: Always
Usually
Often
Rarely

questions.correctAnswerText: Rarely
questions.explanation: You will rarely hear a flat tire. Instead, you'll notice a sudden change in how the motorcycle handles.

questions.question: If you must ride over an obstacle, you should:

options.text: Slow down as much as possible.
Lean the motorcycle to one side.
Speed up if you can.
Stay on your seat and lift your feet off the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as much as possible.
questions.explanation: Slow down and hit the obstacle at a 90-degree angle if possible. Keep your motorcycle upright. Just before impact, ease off the throttle to lighten the front wheel.

questions.question: Braking while turning is:

options.text: Easier than braking on a straight road.
Harder than braking on a straight road.
Safe using only the front brake.
Safe using only the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Harder than braking on a straight road.
questions.explanation: Braking while turning is more difficult than braking on a straight road. You can use both brakes, but you need proper technique and great care.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Reduce your speed.
Increase your distance from other vehicles.
Reduce your distance from other vehicles.
Use your high beam light when possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your distance from other vehicles.
questions.explanation: At night, slow down and increase your distance from other vehicles. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther. Use your high beam, except when following or meeting another vehicle.

questions.question: When riding in a group, motorcyclists should:

options.text: Not worry about space cushions.
Increase their space cushions.
Cut their space cushions in half.
Keep enough space around each rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep enough space around each rider.
questions.explanation: Ride close together as a group, but always keep enough space around each rider for safety.

questions.question: Over-the-counter drugs like cold tablets:

options.text: Can reduce your ability to safely ride.
Probably won't affect your riding ability.
Don't create any risk to your riding.
Are always safe to take before riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can reduce your ability to safely ride.
questions.explanation: All drugs, including over-the-counter medicines, can affect your ability to ride safely. Know the side effects before you take any drug and ride.

questions.question: When braking, you should:

options.text: Always use both brakes.
Use only the front brake.
Use only the rear brake on wet roads.
Use only the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use both brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop, no matter what the road conditions are.
